races.name: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Atlantic Gamble
runners_data.note: Consistent but modest performer on good ground with six runs at this trip; a genuine hold-up horse who will be squeezed into a midfield slot in this traffic-heavy field, limiting the clean passage this style requires to be effective.

runners_data.name: Columbus
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the ride for Mullins and that combination commands respect; placed on good ground over an adequate trip, Columbus has enough tactical speed to find a comfortable midfield berth and pick up late if the pace is true.

runners_data.name: Godsend
runners_data.note: Remarkably strong flat-race profile with three successive wins on good ground, but has not run in 399 days and hurdling technique over Irish obstacles is an enormous unknown; if the jumping holds, this profile is tailor-made for a strongly-run maiden on good going.

runners_data.name: Leader Allen
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained and lightly raced with a form string that hints at ability, but 465 days off the track and unknown going to style makes this a speculative entry; racing style is unclassified, so positional flexibility may work in a chaotic finale.

runners_data.name: Lincoln Mill
runners_data.note: Notable fade flag in the form data suggests this horse doesn't see out the trip strongly; the hold-up role mapped in midfield is secondary to the concern that he may weaken when the race quickens from two out on good ground.

runners_data.name: Tradonthebay
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer up to 3m on good ground and a natural prominent racer; 26 days since last run keeps him fresh, and he has the stamina to grind on if Young Rebel's pace is modest, though his ceiling looks limited at OR 93.

runners_data.name: Tyson Fury
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with good recent form including two seconds, ran just five days ago which is a significant concern for freshness; sits naturally prominent and will likely push Young Rebel hardest in the early stages, potentially injecting pace that suits late runners.

runners_data.name: Young Rebel
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, trained by Emmet Mullins with Harry Cobden booked — that partnership suggests this horse is expected to be competitive; won on soft ground and stepping up from 16f to 2m1f is the key query, but an uncontested lead flatters the chance enormously.

runners_data.name: Eastwatch
runners_data.note: Flat background showing placed form on good ground; dropped into hurdles and mapped to midfield despite being a genuine hold-up type — the four-year-old will likely race closer than comfortable, which works against the patient tactics that suit his profile.

runners_data.name: Finjimk
runners_data.note: Three successive finishes of seventh or eighth on good ground with a fade flag attached; a true hold-up horse positioned into midfield by traffic, and the fade tendency combined with racing out of role makes a big run hard to construct.

runners_data.name: Golden Handshake
runners_data.note: Impressive flat pedigree including two wins on good ground; a hold-up horse with genuine class on this surface, and 317 days off the track is the only credible deterrent to this profile suiting the shape perfectly.

runners_data.name: Hinchinbrooke
runners_data.note: Headgear noted; placed on flat on good ground and steps to hurdling with a prominent style that fits this race shape well; 22 days since last run and a stable that is 0/9 in the past fortnight tempers expectation, but the tactical position is correct.

runners_data.name: The Flying Rambler
runners_data.note: Very lightly raced with two runs both in heavy or testing conditions; unclassified style and headgear flagged — the step to good ground at 2m1f over hurdles is a significant move into the unknown.

runners_data.name: Youknowthecode
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott, which is always relevant context; the fade flag and recent poor form (8-6-0 latest) suggest the Elliott yard hasn't found the key yet, and stepping back from heavy/heavy-soft to good may not solve it.

runners_data.name: Banphrionsa Alainn
runners_data.note: Single run showing — finished 11th on heavy — and 187 days off; a genuine hold-up type who has the fade flag attached and will be pushed into traffic closer than ideal in this race shape, making a bold effort structurally difficult.

runners_data.name: Everyday Life
runners_data.note: Headgear noted; ran ninth on good ground last time, and a natural hold-up performer who will be shuffled forward by traffic; the fade flag compounds the concern that racing out of position will blunt whatever ability this horse possesses.

runners_data.name: Mystery Decision
runners_data.note: Form shows a fall and a blank, going is unknown, and the amateur jockey booking for a 7-year-old in a 23-runner maiden hurdle raises questions; too many unknowns to assess with confidence.

runners_data.name: Rumble Demosa
runners_data.note: Two runs, both seventh at 19f on good ground — consistent placement but no sign of progress and a stable that is 0/5 in the past fortnight; a hold-up horse with no obvious reason to reverse recent form in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Tiktok Casey
runners_data.note: Won on heavy/soft ground and placed on heavy; the step to good going is an interrogation point, but a prominent style fits this race shape and the form line includes a win at 16f — trip is fine if the surface suits.

runners_data.name: Thedreamistilalive
runners_data.note: Finished ninth on good ground last time over 16f and carries a fade flag; a four-year-old in first season over hurdles with a very small sample and a trainer who is 0/2 in the past fortnight — hard to build a case.

runners_data.name: Rene's Gold
runners_data.note: 447 days off the track, going is unknown, and form reads P/7 — a very thin basis for assessment in a 23-runner field; the lightly raced flag and long absence make this one of the most speculative entries in the race.

runners_data.name: Leva Deva
runners_data.note: Ran 14th and an unknown finish both on good ground over 18f; the fade flag is present and no jockey listed is a procedural concern — everything about this entry points to a well-beaten outcome.

runners_data.name: Digby Bridge
runners_data.note: Completely unknown — no jockey listed, no form, no going assessment; the Barry Connell yard has had one winner from five in the past fortnight and the horse could be anything, which makes it a live dark horse only in a total pace collapse.

races.paceDynamic: Young Rebel is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 23-strong maiden hurdle and, with no natural rival to push him from the front, Harry Cobden can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop around Galway's undulating track. The pace will be genuine but not frantic — Young Rebel sets an honest rhythm from the flag, with Tyson Fury, Hinchinbrooke, Tiktok Casey and Tradonthebay pressing from prominent positions just off the shoulder, creating a race run at a steady-to-fair tempo that is unlikely to be punishing enough to shred the field. This shape — an uncontested leader, a bunched prominent group, and a long tail of hold-up horses strung behind — classically favours horses who can travel in the first four or five and produce a clean jump at the last, rather than those who must make up ground from the rear. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Finjimk, Eastwatch, Everyday Life, Banphrionsa Alainn and Atlantic Gamble are all genuine hold-up performers who will be forced to race further forward than is natural, compressing the midfield and making the race look falsely well-strung; the horses most likely to genuinely secure their preferred position are Columbus, Godsend and Golden Handshake, all of whom have the tactical flexibility to find a comfortable spot. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent-to-midfield runners who travel smoothly behind a single controlled pace-setter and have proven aptitude on good ground are the profile this shape rewards.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Young Rebel Dictates Comfortably
scenarios.trigger: If Young Rebel is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the prominent group cannot sustain a meaningful challenge over the final two flights.
scenarios.body: Young Rebel sets a controlled tempo with Cobden fully in charge, the race developing into a test of jumping accuracy and finishing quality rather than stamina; horses who travel in the slipstream with their jumping intact come into play at the second-last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent-to-midfield horses tracks Young Rebel close enough to strike turning for home and outstays him in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: With the gallop honest but not brutal, a horse with a high cruising speed who sits third or fourth and attacks from two out has the ideal scenario; Godsend's strong flat form on good ground makes him a prime candidate if his jumping holds up after 399 days off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Makes Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough in the middle third to stretch the field and create space for a late run from off the pace.
scenarios.body: True hold-up performers like Columbus and Golden Handshake benefit if the bunched prominent group injects pace approaching the final bend, creating a two-length gap that rewards a sweeping finish; however, several nominally hold-up types here are redistribution candidates forced forward, meaning genuine closers are fewer than the field size suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse — Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Young Rebel gets outpaced or makes a critical jumping error, leaving no leader and triggering a scrambled, ragged finish.
scenarios.body: With no reliable backup pace-setter, the field could bunch dangerously at the final two hurdles and a rough-jumping maiden-hurdle finish unfolds; unexposed runners with flat-track form like Leader Allen or Digby Bridge could capitalise on the chaos if they have tracked close enough.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tyson Fury's early exertion — running just five days after his last outing, if he presses Young Rebel hard from the first flight he could inject a pace spike that burns himself out and leaves the race wide open from two out.

Godsend is 399 days off the track and has no hurdle form on record; if his jumping is clean he is a major player, but a fumble at an early flight in a 23-runner field could trigger a chaotic pile-up involving the entire midfield bunch.

Columbus and Golden Handshake are both genuine hold-up types with strong form credentials who will be forced marginally closer than ideal by traffic — watch whether Townend and O'Brien can find a clear run on the inside or outside turning in, as a blocked passage here is a real risk in a field this size.

The bunched midfield created by so many redistributed hold-up horses racing out of role means the second-last hurdle will be jumped by 15+ runners almost simultaneously — watch for interference, stumbles and carried-wide incidents that could derail prominent-positioned horses at the critical moment.

Young Rebel's jumping accuracy over the Galway undulations is the single biggest race-shape variable — if he gets low at any of the first three hurdles, the race could lose its sole pace anchor entirely and devolve into a messy, falsely-run contest.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Galway Tribes Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Path d'Oroux
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Cromwell and Donoghue who has solid Good-ground form (8/15 sim-going) and stays this trip well; at 9 years old the concern is a declining peak, but if the pace plays perfectly into late runners this horse is ideally positioned off the back of the field.

runners_data.name: Putapoundinthejar
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, back just two days after its last run which is a fitness query, but A J Martin's record here is solid; its chance rests entirely on dictating a controlled gallop — if it gets it, the STYLE_FIT flag is less relevant, but it is genuinely racing at the outer edge of its comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Paul's Dream
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with recent back-to-back wins on Good and strong sim-going figures (11/15); Danny Mullins adds meaningful riding quality in a busy field, and the 22-day layoff is ideal freshness — one of the likelier prominent types to actually secure the position it wants.

runners_data.name: Autumn Twist
runners_data.note: A five-year-old with a recent second on this trip in Good going and a good trainer strike rate (2/26 over 14 days); the claim jockey is a risk in a 22-runner competitive handicap where positioning in the early scramble is critical.

runners_data.name: Matt Connor
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who wears a hood and has two wins on Good ground; best form has come at shorter trips (10f win, 18f win on Heavy) and the 20f second-last run was poor, so stamina at 2m1f in a strung-out race is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Red Glory
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's consistent prominent horse with outstanding sim-going figures (13/15) and a recent Good-ground win at 2m; Darragh O'Keeffe is a top booking and this horse's profile makes it one of the most likely to actually win the positional battle early.

runners_data.name: Fiveonefive
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride on this hold-up type who has decent Good-ground form (3rd and 4th in recent GOO runs) and stays trips up to 2m6f; wears a hood and the 11-day turnaround is fine — a genuine beneficiary if the pace scenario plays out for closers.

runners_data.name: Slurricane
runners_data.note: Prominent racer on paper but sim-going record is modest (6/15) and there are no wins to speak of; with only a 7lb claimer in the saddle and 230 days since any meaningful form, this horse is unlikely to secure the prominent position it wants in such a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Spy
runners_data.note: Two wins on Good ground and a prominent style that has worked on similar going; the 28-day freshness is reasonable, but trainer C Byrnes has a limited string and competing for front positions in a 22-runner field with a 5lb claimer makes this harder than its OR of 122 suggests.

runners_data.name: Wholelotofbusiness
runners_data.note: Has won twice on Good over this sort of trip and wears a tongue-tie; the 61-day absence is the primary concern, and while it wants to race prominently, the layoff may blunt its early sharpness when position is fiercely contested.

runners_data.name: Avalo
runners_data.note: Strong Good-ground record (12/14 sim-going) with two wins and a second over similar trips — genuinely a prominent-style horse by nature, but with so many traffic-seekers ahead of it, this one is likely to be shuffled back from where it wants to race; STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence in a crowded scenario.

runners_data.name: Come On The Lads
runners_data.note: Cromwell's second string in this race, a prominent type whose best form came in softer ground (SOF win) and whose recent Good-ground runs have been well below that; the trainer's yard has multiple runners here but this one has the thinnest recent evidence.

runners_data.name: Kimi De Mai
runners_data.note: Paul Townend is a marquee booking for Mullins and this horse places consistently in Staying company; however its Good-ground record is effectively blank (1/6 sim-going, no wins), making it a risk despite the jockey upgrade and 118-day freshen-up.

runners_data.name: No Looking Back
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with headgear (b, t) who has been beaten a long way in recent runs on Good and Heavy; the 91-day break and modest form string (P0430-) suggest this is on a retrieval mission rather than a winning one.

runners_data.name: Jetoile
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up type that won over 2m4f on Good and was placed at Galway; the age is a natural concern but recent form includes a win and a third and the sim-going figures (10/15) are respectable — if closers are rewarded, this veteran cannot be entirely dismissed.

runners_data.name: Arcland
runners_data.note: Three wins on Good ground and strong sim-going (13/15) mark this Cromwell horse out as a genuinely consistent performer; it wants to race prominently by nature but the field depth means it is likely to find itself in midfield — its chance is better than the map position implies but is constrained by that crowd.

runners_data.name: Minella Post
runners_data.note: Recent form includes a fall (F) and several mid-table finishes; naturally a prominent-style horse that will struggle to hold position in this 22-runner scramble, and trainer Thomas Gibney's record over 14 days is quiet — limited upside here.

runners_data.name: Serienmond
runners_data.note: Won on Good at 2m over hurdles and has Good-ground form in the bank, but 230 days off the track is a severe concern; a true prominent racer by inclination who will find this field's positional dynamics working against it after such a lengthy absence.

runners_data.name: Lips Freedom
runners_data.note: Hold-up type tagged with a finish-fade warning and a tongue-tie; two recent wins (GOO and SOF) suggest ability is present, but the ⚠ flag is critical — in a race where closers need a strong late surge, a horse that fades is difficult to trust.

runners_data.name: Berto Ramirez
runners_data.note: A four-year-old hold-up type for Andrew McNamara who won over 2m on Good; unexposed at this level and the youth and lightly-raced profile make it an improver, though 2m1f in a 22-runner hurdle is a significant step up in competition.

runners_data.name: Eye Of A Tiger
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 2m on Good for John Patrick Ryan, whose 14-day record is active (3/25); a true hold-up horse pushed to the midfield map, meaning its natural late-race running could be compromised by getting trapped — STYLE_FIT discount applies.

runners_data.name: Metamorpheus
runners_data.note: Placed three times in recent form including a second on Good, this Andrew McNamara hold-up type has shown consistency; like Eye Of A Tiger it is mapped out of its natural rear position and would need a perfectly run race to produce its best late effort.

races.paceDynamic: Putapoundinthejar is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with just two days since its last run, will stride to the front and attempt to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop — there is no natural challenger to push it wide or force a contested lead. The problem is that Paul's Dream, Red Glory, Autumn Twist, Spy, Slurricane, Wholelotoftheobusiness, Come On The Lads and Kimi De Mai all want to race prominently, meaning the first two furlongs will see a fierce scramble for position that could paradoxically string the field out early even behind a single leader. The field holds substantially more genuine front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred berth; of those, Paul's Dream, Red Glory and Autumn Twist look most capable of actually pressing into the first two or three, while Avalo, Arcland, Serienmond and Minella Post — all true prominent horses — are pushed back into a midfield mapping that does not reflect where they want to be. With a lone leader setting a measured tempo on Good ground over 2m1f and the pace genuinely compressed into mid-division, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with a strong late kick who can bypass the positional chaos, finish powerfully from the back through tired rivals and exploit a steadily-run first half.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Putapoundinthejar dictates unchallenged and the prominent pack fail to close the gap from mid-race.
scenarios.body: Putapoundinthejar sets fractions it controls entirely, the prominent scramblers burn energy jostling for position, and it arrives at the final flight with enough in reserve to hold on; horses who tracked just off the pace without expending too much in the early melee are the main dangers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent traffic jam burns out the chasers and the true hold-up horses power home from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Path d'Oroux, Fiveonefive and Jetoile settle comfortably in the rear, avoid the early pushing-and-shoving, and launch sustained finishing runs from the home turn on Good ground that their profiles are built for; genuine hold-up horses with strong GOO records are the clear beneficiaries here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Grinds Through
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent types secures an economical tracking position early and quickens clear from the last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Red Glory or Paul's Dream — both with strong Good-ground form and recent wins — tuck in second or third without burning excessive energy during the positional battle and use class to sprint clear late; this is the scenario where a high-RPR prominent type with a strong same-going record converts position into victory.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses; Muddle-Through
scenarios.trigger: If Putapoundinthejar is overhauled early and pace becomes ragged, producing a rough-and-tumble affair decided by fitness and opportunism.
scenarios.body: An unusually flat finish where the winner comes from an unfashionable position mid-division, possibly a redistributed prominent horse who ends up with an accidental split-rail run; Arcland, with its strong Good-ground record and Cromwell handling, or Berto Ramirez as a lightly-raced young improver, could exploit the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Putapoundinthejar's ability to control early fractions is the single most important variable — if it is immediately harassed by Paul's Dream or Red Glory off the gate, the controlled-pace scenario unravels and the entire race shape changes.

With 22 runners, all prominent-style horses scrambling for the front five or six positions in the opening quarter-mile, interference and early crowding are a serious risk — watch for Arcland, Avalo and Serienmond being shuffled back and losing significant ground before the first hurdle.

Serienmond has been off the track for 230 days and Wholelotofbusiness for 61 days — both want prominent positions that require peak early energy; if either tires from their layoff mid-race, they could impede horses trying to improve through the field.

Lips Freedom's finish-fade flag is particularly relevant if the pace is genuinely modest — a slow-run race ending in a sprint finish is exactly the scenario where this horse's tendency to weaken late becomes most damaging to its chances.

Paul Townend's booking for Kimi De Mai is the single most significant jockey move in the race — monitor its market move and whether Mullins has signalled confidence with a fresh horse that has rarely been tested on Good ground at this trip.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Handicap Hurdle (Listed)

runners_data.name: American Mike
runners_data.note: Strongly suited by this 2m6½f trip on Good ground, winning over 24f Good last time before a fair second at Cheltenham; Josh Williamson claims 5lb for Olly Murphy who has had a quiet 14-day spell (0/13); hold-up style is a structural advantage in this compressed field.

runners_data.name: Pinot Gris
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter in a 22-strong field; De Bromhead has 7 from 43 in the last 14 days and the horse won over 20f Good at the course recently, though the style-fit tag (0.91) acknowledges she typically races more prominently than a pure leader.

runners_data.name: Sir Galahad
runners_data.note: In excellent form with two recent wins over 20f Good and Jack Kennedy aboard is a significant plus; Olly Murphy's runners are a touch quiet (0/13 last 14 days) but Sir Galahad's prominent style and class at OR 136 make him a natural threat in a race that suits the position.

runners_data.name: Double Powerful
runners_data.note: Last ran 104 days ago which is the longest absence among the principals; placed at 25f on Good and comfortable off this trip, but the long break for Neil Mulholland (3/10 in 14 days) and a prominent style in a crowded field makes securing a berth harder.

runners_data.name: Dream On Baby
runners_data.note: Won over 21f Good and placed twice over this sort of distance, wears hood/tongue-tie combination; Emmet Mullins has had a productive 14 days (1/11) and Donagh Meyler is a capable handler of big-field handicaps, though the horse has to navigate traffic from a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Bunting
runners_data.note: W P Mullins' hold-up type that has shown flashes over 20f Good but recent form reads 4-9-9-9-6 so no wins in that sequence; Danny Mullins takes the ride and the late-running profile gives tactical flexibility in a 22-runner field, though the horse needs to improve on recent outings.

runners_data.name: Comfort Zone
runners_data.note: Ran just five days ago which is the shortest gap of any runner here; OR 131 and listed as a prominent runner who fades in the finish, making the heavy race load a concern — Joseph Patrick O'Brien has been in prolific form (14/72 in 14 days) but the quick turnaround tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Dani Donadoni
runners_data.note: Paul Townend in the saddle is the standout booking for this race; the six-year-old has placed at OR 128 over 24f Good and 16f Good, consistent in his best form, though the W P Mullins team is represented here rather than in the more glamorous slots, worth respecting.

runners_data.name: Stede Bonnet
runners_data.note: A five-year-old with two wins and two seconds in last five, ridden by a 5lb claimer (James Smith) which helps carry 154lbs; won over 16f Soft and placed over 20f, so the 2m6½f trip on Good represents a step into the unknown for the Gordon Elliott-trained runner.

runners_data.name: Ambitious Fellow
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old wearing a hood, falling and unseated in his last two runs — clearly going through a difficult patch; Peter Fahey has modest 14-day numbers (1/9) and the horse's good-going form (0 wins in 13 similar-going runs) gives little encouragement at this level.

runners_data.name: Grann's Boy
runners_data.note: Won twice over 22f Good and has placed prominently at this sort of trip; H Rogers has a small operation (1/3 in 14 days) and Sean Flanagan is an experienced pilot in Irish handicaps, but recent form of 9-10-6-2-2 shows he's been running into things rather than winning.

runners_data.name: Ifiwerearichman
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old with a prominent style and headgear, last seen placing at 23f Good; Paul Nolan sends three horses to this race (0/14 in 14 days) so the trainer's form is subdued, and Eoin Staples claiming 5lb helps the weight, though the horse has not won in recent memory.

runners_data.name: Mousey Brown
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old wearing a tongue-tie, twice placed over 24f Good and consistent in that company; Patrick M O'Brien claims 5lb and the trainer (McLoughlin) has a quiet book (0/5 in 14 days), but the hold-up style is genuinely useful here if the pace holds up throughout.

runners_data.name: Koori Star
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer by nature at OR 123, but with ten or more horses ahead of him in the pecking order for early positions this has to race further back than ideal — Brian Hayes is a capable tactician who may find a way through, and the 133-day absence is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Gin Tonic
runners_data.note: Won over 20f Good and placed at the same distance, a naturally prominent type whose real position has been pushed back due to field congestion; Paul Nolan's subdued 14-day record (0/14) and two recent pulled-up runs in soft make this an obvious query, though the Good ground brings them back into play.

runners_data.name: Kiltealy Park
runners_data.note: Won at 24f Good most recently and is a genuine front-running type at heart — the redistribution to midfield reflects the impossibility of every prominent horse getting its position, not any doubt about the horse's preference; Alan O'Sullivan claims 5lb for the prolific Nolan yard.

runners_data.name: Sequoiaspirit
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old winner over 20f Soft most recently and a front-running preference that cannot be accommodated given the prominent logjam in this field; Ray Hackett has a tiny book (0/1 in 14 days) and wears a tongue-tie — the horse needs luck from the back in a way that doesn't suit its natural game.

runners_data.name: Ad Caelum
runners_data.note: Placed three times over 22-24f Good including a win at 24f Good, a consistent late-runner for J J Slevin; John Patrick Ryan has been active (3/25 in 14 days) and the hold-up style at OR 121 makes this one of the more naturally positioned runners in the field for the race shape that develops.

runners_data.name: Minella Diamond
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winner at 20f Soft and Good, in smart form at OR 120; a naturally prominent runner whose position has been pushed into the midfield mapping by the sheer volume of similar types — if Danny Mullins can negotiate a forward berth early, the recent winning form is directly relevant.

runners_data.name: Burning Ability
runners_data.note: Won over 20f Good and placed at 24f Good, showing a genuine affinity for this type of surface and distance; the redistribution to midfield reflects competitive pressure at the front of the race rather than any style preference change — Eoin Christopher McCarthy has been modestly active (2/9 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: From The Ashes
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old winner over 24f Good in most recent start, returning after 199 days which is the longest break in the field — trainer C Byrnes has sent no runners in the last 14 days and the long layoff for a veteran jumper on return to a 22-horse Listed race requires caution; a true prominent type racing effectively back due to field congestion.

runners_data.name: Elusive Ogie
runners_data.note: A five-year-old with modest form figures of 5-10-P-0-5 over similar trips on Good ground, and all 11 recent similar-going runs have ended without a win; last ran just 15 days ago and no jockey is listed publicly, which is an information gap for a horse that is already a long way down the pecking order.

races.paceDynamic: Pinot Gris is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 22-horse field and, crucially, faces no meaningful pressure for the lead — she can dictate her own rhythm through what should be an honest but controlled gallop over 2m6½f on Good ground. The pack behind her is dominated by prominent-types, many of whom cannot all achieve their natural position: Sir Galahad, Double Powerful, Dream On Baby, Dani Donadoni, Stede Bonnet and Comfort Zone will jostle for the handful of spots directly in her wake, creating a compressed, bustling mid-division rather than a genuine hunt for the lead. Hold-up horses American Mike, Bunting, Ad Caelum and Mousey Brown will settle towards the rear of a large field that is likely to string out on this galloping track. The field holds more genuinely prominent types than the race shape can accommodate, with Koori Star, Sequoiaspirit, Kiltealy Park, Gin Tonic and several others likely to find themselves racing further back than ideal — those who can genuinely settle off a sustainable pace and produce a finishing kick from mid-to-rear will be best placed, giving hold-up and late-running profiles a structural edge in this race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pinot Gris controls, stays fresh
scenarios.trigger: If Pinot Gris is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent pack immediately behind fails to mount a sustained challenge in the home straight.
scenarios.body: Pinot Gris bowls along at her own pace, conserving energy over the 2m6½f trip, and arrives at the final two hurdles with untapped reserves while the prominent battle behind her has taken a toll on her rivals; the six-year-old's recent win over this course at Good going is directly relevant.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses storm late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack pushes a strong enough pace that Pinot Gris is pressed beyond comfort, setting up a truly run race for the closers to pounce.
scenarios.body: American Mike, who won over 24f on Good and is in strong form, and Ad Caelum, a consistent closer with multiple Good-ground placings at this trip, are ideally positioned to sweep through a tiring field in the final climb; Bunting, held up for W P Mullins, could also arrive late if the pace has genuinely been honest throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent scrimmage, one prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types — Sir Galahad, Double Powerful, Dream On Baby and Dani Donadoni — creates enough internal competition to produce a genuinely run race that a prominent survivor can win.
scenarios.body: With Paul Townend aboard Dani Donadoni and Jack Kennedy on Sir Galahad, both trainers send top-class pilots who can manage a crowded prominent berth and find the best position available; if one of these can sit just off Pinot Gris and conserve enough energy, the trip and Good going suit both.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed type beats the map
scenarios.trigger: If one of the genuinely prominent horses mapped back — Kiltealy Park, Burning Ability or Minella Diamond — manages to secure closer to their natural position than the pace map projects and the race is slowly run enough to reward early positioning.
scenarios.body: Kiltealy Park won on Good over 24f at her most recent start and is a true front-running type who could benefit if the field fans wide early; Minella Diamond, a back-to-back winner, would be dangerous if allowed to race closer to the pace than her redistributed slot suggests.

watchPoints.text: Comfort Zone ran just five days ago and fades in finishes — if the pace becomes intense in the final mile, watch for this runner to drop away sharply and cause interference in a tightly packed 22-horse field.

races.paceDynamic: Saliba is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push them, will dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop around Galway's tight 1m½f track. Gliondar and Bang Bang are the natural prominent types best placed to sit just behind Saliba and use the controlled tempo to their advantage. The field carries more hold-up inclination than the race shape can accommodate — Chloe's Boy, Tijuana, and Romantic War are true closers who are likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than ideal given the lack of early pressure, blunting their natural finishes. A sustainable, front-dictated tempo on Good ground over this straight-ish Galway trip strongly favours prominent racers who can lob in behind Saliba and produce their effort without having to make up ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Saliba Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Saliba controls the pace unchallenged and sets a steady, sustainable gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Gliondar or Bang Bang sit close to the pace from the off, travel comfortably through the race, and produce a clean burst in the closing stages without needing to make significant ground; a steady tempo means the front rank is never softened up for closers to exploit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Saliba Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is so conservative that Saliba simply outstays everything from the front and the field cannot reel them in.
scenarios.body: Saliba, never seriously tested, idles in front and the modest gallop leaves those behind with too much to do from off the pace; prominent runners who have travelled best are second-best but the winner is already gone.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Stayer Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Saliba sets a stronger-than-expected gallop and the race develops into an honest staying test up the straight.
scenarios.body: Runners with genuine stamina for this extended mile trip who have travelled in midfield come into their own as the pace takes its toll on those who have led or pressed too hard; horses whose form profile shows they stay well and appreciate Good ground are rewarded.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brisk enough to soften up the front-runners and the hold-up horses manage to find a clear run in the straight.
scenarios.body: Although Chloe's Boy, Tijuana, and Romantic War are true hold-up types, the map suggests they will be racing further forward than ideal, reducing the likelihood they produce a genuine late swoop; the scenario is possible but structurally undermined by the field's redistribution of closing types.

watchPoints.text: Gliondar is the horse to track in the early stages — if J M Sheridan slots in smoothly just off Saliba, the prominent style and O'Brien trainer angle make them the most likely beneficiary of a controlled tempo.
Saliba's style-fit flag at 1m½f is worth monitoring in the straight — if they begin to idle or shorten stride after the turn, Bang Bang and Gliondar are best positioned to pounce.

Chloe's Boy, Tijuana, and Romantic War are all natural closers who will be pressed forward by the compressed field shape — watch whether any secure a clean passage in the straight or whether they become traffic problems for one another.

Storzando (Wesley Joyce, 3lb claim) is lightly raced and stepping up in trip — if the pace is genuine enough to stretch the field, an unexposed profile with staying potential could make late ground worth noting.

Rest Your Mind's 278-day absence is the longest in the field — watch the market moves closer to post time, as any meaningful support for the O'Leary runner would suggest a confident home signal despite the significant layoff.

races.paceDynamic: The Sweet Escape is the lone confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, critically, faces no serious pressure for the lead — she can roll out from the gates and control tempo at a rate entirely of her own choosing on Good ground over seven furlongs. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses, but many of those — Rhythm King, Navagio, Lough Leane, Gloriously Glam, and Mytimetoshine — are genuine closers who cannot all find their natural position in this configuration and will be shuffled into an artificial midfield berth, diluting the late kick the race would otherwise produce. Bay Of Dreams, Faoladh, Chester Nimitz, Mickey The Steel, and Minaun View will press forward into prominent positions behind The Sweet Escape, creating a logical racing order but with a measured, sustainable gallop rather than a true searching test. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: a single uncontested front-runner setting her own pace on Good turf over seven furlongs heavily favours prominently-ridden horses who can travel in her slipstream and pounce in the straight, rather than true hold-up horses who need a fast pace to set up a late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If The Sweet Escape dictates an uncontested, even tempo and the field fails to close the gap before the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The Sweet Escape rolls along without a single horse threatening her lead through the first half of the race, and the prominent runners tracking her — Bay Of Dreams, Minaun View, Mickey The Steel — are best positioned to challenge in the straight as closers run out of ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Bay Of Dreams or Minaun View travel powerfully just off The Sweet Escape and wear her down entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop suits horses who can sit a length or two off the pace and produce a sustained challenge in the straight without needing a sprint-ending kick; both Bay Of Dreams and Minaun View have strong recent form at this course and distance configuration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Breaks Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply in the final quarter-mile, compressing the field and giving a well-positioned midfield horse a clear run through.
scenarios.body: Gloriously Glam or Spent All Me Money, operating just off the front group, would benefit most if traffic clears and they get a clean passage; both have winning form on Good ground and are sufficiently close to the pace to matter.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave the hold-up horses with daylight in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely outcome given the lone front-runner's ability to control tempo and the fact that most natural closers here — Rhythm King, Navagio, Lough Leane — have been redistributed into midfield and are unlikely to get a clean late run from their true preferred position.

watchPoints.text: The Sweet Escape's ability to get uncontested lead is the race-shaping moment — if she rolls clear from the gates without any of the prominent runners (Bay Of Dreams, Faoladh) pushing her, the race is hers to lose.

Minaun View has won twice in its last three starts on Good ground and races at a prominent pace — without a declared jockey confirmed in the data, any late rider change or market move should be noted closely.

Rhythm King ran just two days ago, which is an unusually quick turnaround for a hold-up horse in an 18-runner field; monitor its market and Gavin Ryan's pre-race body language for signs the run is merely a fitness exercise.

Gloriously Glam is a three-time winner on Good ground and Shane Foley rides — if it can secure a prominent pitch rather than its natural hold-up position in the early stages, its chance improves markedly beyond what the style tag implies.

With seven or more horses effectively compressed into an artificial midfield, traffic and a clean passage in the final two furlongs will be critical — horses drawn on the outside who can race wider (Mickey The Steel, Bay Of Dreams) may avoid the worst of the scrimmage.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Saxo is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner field and, racing on Good ground over 1m4f at Galway, is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop with no genuine pace rival likely to chase them down from the outset. The prominent slots behind Royal Saxo are heavily contested: Diamond Exchange, Thatwilldoso, Unterberg, Daonethatgotaway, Deralo Ir, Granville Street, and Pillar Of Hope all want to race prominently, but there are far more of them than the race shape can accommodate — of these, Diamond Exchange (Shane Foley, in-form yard), Thatwilldoso (recent winner, consistent), and Unterberg are most likely to actually secure the prominent berths, with others forced to settle deeper than ideal. The field also holds more hold-up types than the rear of the field can absorb, so Sir Jeremy, Concert Party, and Arch Enemy have been redistributed to midfield and will not be operating in their true comfort zone. With one honest pacer and a single-file Galway track, this race shape strongly favours tractable, prominent-to-midfield runners who can travel within striking distance and quicken in the straight rather than deep closers who need a strong pace to reel in the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Pacer Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Saxo bowls along uncontested at a fair but not brutal gallop and the prominent pack settle within range without disrupting the tempo.
scenarios.body: Royal Saxo controls every yard, and the lack of a pace duel means the prominent runners immediately behind who travel sweetly are gifted a perfect setup — they make their challenge in the straight with legs still under them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent-types causes early crowding and jostling that lifts the tempo in the first half-mile, setting up a more genuine gallop.
scenarios.body: The elevated early pace stretches the field and benefits those sitting third to sixth who can switch off and accelerate once the scrimmage settles — Galway's turning track punishes those who use energy fighting for position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough through the middle stages that the genuine hold-up horses tracking further back get a true run to aim at.
scenarios.body: Superficial (recent winner, 56-day break, strong form on Good) and Fratas (consistent placed record) can produce a late run if the field comes back to them, though many horses mapped at the rear are not true hold-up types so the pace may not be strong enough to set this up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes traffic issues, interference, or Royal Saxo weakens sharply having gone too hard for conditions, scrambling the result.
scenarios.body: A runner who has been shuffled wide or finds daylight in the straight at a big price — Arch Enemy (two recent wins, Good ground form) or Steps In The Sand (course-distance profile) could emerge from the chaos of a bunched field.

watchPoints.text: Royal Saxo sets the entire tempo alone — if Robbie Colgan elects to dawdle in front, the pack will compress and the race turns into a sprint, wiping out its own chance and gifting the contest to a prominent handler like Diamond Exchange or Thatwilldoso.

The prominent group (Diamond Exchange, Thatwilldoso, Unterberg, Daonethatgotaway, Granville Street) all want to sit 2nd-6th on Galway's tight track — watch for bumping and positional battles in the first two furlongs that could unbalance any of them.

Arch Enemy ran just two days ago and Steps In The Sand is a natural prominent type forced back — both are worth watching for any early signs of restlessness or reluctance to settle in unnatural positions.

Superficial returns from 56 days off with a recent win on Good — watch whether W J Lee is patient enough to sit mid-to-rear and produce a late run, or whether the horse is keen early, which would compromise the hold-up plan.

The redistributed hold-up horses (Sir Jeremy, Concert Party, Arch Enemy) are all mapped to midfield — watch at the 3f pole whether they get a clear passage or become caught in traffic as the race quickens on Galway's turning straight.
